case_name: Smt. Rajeshwari vs Jugal Kishore Gupta
facts_of_case: The parties were married under Hindu rites and customs. The respondent suffered from epilepsy. The petitioner discovered this and sought to annul the marriage. The respondent returned to her parents' house after a few years. The trial court passed an ex parte decree of divorce.

legal_principles.principle: A spouse who has won in the High Court and got a decree of dissolution of marriage cannot by marrying immediately after the High Court's judgment take away the right of presenting an application for special leave to appeal from the other spouse.
legal_principles.held: The successful party must wait for a reasonable time and make sure whether an application for special leave has been filed in the Supreme Court.
cited_cases: Tejinder Kaur v. Gurmit Singh, AIR 1988 SC 839
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — to ensure fairness in the appeal process

legal_principles.principle: A remarriage even during the pendency of an application for setting aside an ex parte decree for dissolution would be valid unless the applicant has obtained an interim order of injunction.
legal_principles.held: It does not provide for the case of an application for setting aside an ex parte decree for dissolution which would be competent under the Code of Civil Procedure.
cited_cases: Smt. Lila Gupta v. Laxmi Narain, AIR 1978 SC 1351
Smt. Varsha Gadrey v. Vilas Gadrey, F. A. No. 131 of 1979
legal_principles.significance: MEDIUM — to clarify the effect of an ex parte decree
